entry.title: Zoominoes v0.1.0.post4
entry.content:
Community testing build. Feedback and bug reports welcome.
## Install
**1. BepInEx** — download **BepInEx 6 bleeding-edge, `Unity.Mono`, `win-x64`** from <https://builds.bepinex.dev/projects/bepinex_be> and unzip it into the game folder, next to `Zoominoes.exe`. Zoominoes is a Unity 6 Mono game; BepInEx 5 will not work. Run the game once so BepInEx creates its folders, then close it.
e.g. for Windows: <https://builds.bepinex.dev/projects/bepinex_be/785/BepInEx-Unity.Mono-win-x64-6.0.0-be.785%2B6abdba4.zip>
**2. The mod** — unzip `ZoominoesArchipelago.zip` into the same game folder. It drops into `BepInEx/plugins/`.
**3. The world** — put `zoominoes.apworld` in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
On Linux the game runs under Proton with the same files. Add `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp=n,b" %command%` to the Steam launch options, or the loader will not inject.
## Playing
Press **F1** for the connection panel, enter your server address, port, slot name and password, and connect. The panel opens by itself until you do. Details are remembered for next launch.
Runs are played on a dedicated **AP** profile. Your existing saves are not read or written while the mod is installed.
## What is randomised
Animals, snacks, souvenirs, zookeepers and difficulty tiers arrive as Archipelago items, along with extra starting gold, extra plays and hand size.
`randomize_starter_zookeeper` and `randomize_starter_unlocks` extend that to what you open with: a random zookeeper in place of Marina, and a random 6 animals, 4 snacks and 4 souvenirs in place of Starfish, Fennec and the rest. Whatever the draw passes over becomes an item like anything else.
Checks come from Gift Shop slots and from finishing a day. **Every difficulty tier has its own set of both** — "Tier 3 - Shop 2 - Slot 1" is a different location from "Tier 5 - Shop 2 - Slot 1", so each tier you unlock opens 43 fresh checks: 24 across its eight shops and 19 across its playable days. On top of that, winning with each zookeeper and clearing each tier are checks in their own right.
Three goals: clear a target difficulty tier, clear it with several different zookeepers, or collect Zoo Tickets scattered across the multiworld.
Only normal runs take part — daily challenges, seeded runs and challenge runs are left alone.
Items apply from your **next** run, since the game fixes its content pool when a run begins.
## Options
`Zoominoes-template.yaml` has every option, its documentation and its weights. Put it in your Archipelago `Players` folder and change the name at the top.
Content the seed has no room for is unlocked from the start rather than left unobtainable.

entry.title: Burger Shop v0.3.2
entry.content:
This release contains several QOL updates for both Burger Shop 1 and 2.
- The client will create and manage its own Archipelago save file. This means a new save file is no longer needed for an Archipelago session, you just need to connect the client then load the Archipelago save file in Burger Shop. - Locations sent to Burger Shop will now automatically show that level as a 5-star completion on the map screen. The exceptions to this are level 80 for Burger Shop 1 and Levels 118, 119, and 120 for Burger Shop 2, since they are required to reach the goal. - The zip file containing the game files have been updated to make re-installation easier. You just need to copy over the "archipelago" and "properties" folder into your Burger Shop installation directory and replace all files. - The Burger Shop client windows are now named to make it easier to identify them.
Additionally, - The Old Chap, Dog Lover, and Shirtless Guy customers cannot be placed in level 1 if character randomization is turned on, to prevent the rare case that there are no available levels in logic for the first 15 levels.

entry.title: RE3Remake v0.3.0
entry.content:
This is a "pre-release" of Version 3 that people can test while I'm MIA again. Any bugs you all find please report to the thread, and I'll try to get them fixed up when I get back from my trip 😃
**RE2Randomizer features ported over:** ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
**Enemy kills can be checks/locations** Same as RE2, this adds a lot of checks (and more backtracking) to the randomizer 😃
**Double Weapons / Local Weapons** Same as RE2, always nice to have more weaponry in the world (although you won't receive duplicates, still)
**In-game GUI tooltips when paused/in menu and a more revamped GUI system overall** <- Mod menu is a lot more pleasant to look at
**Safes when checked now behave closer to RE2**, they'll open automatically, the item will poof and the map will clear!
**You can no longer toggle Deathlink on difficulties you have not beaten Vanilla** It's a design choice that I appreciated from RE2, so now we force players to "git gudder" before they can turn it on. I don't want players bringing Inferno Deathlink to a multiworld if they've never beaten the game on Inferno before.
**RE3Randomizer specific changes** ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
**Added "Invisible Enemies"**, which is just as awful as it sounds and can include Nemesis if desired 😅
**Added "Speedy Enemy Mode"**, which is just as awful as it sounds and can include Nemesis if desired 😅
**Added "Enemy Behavior"**, which is just as awful as it sounds and can include Nemesis if desired 😅 [SHOCKEEEEEEEEEEERRRRRR](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sMk-HPBF6Mw) - (you're Shocker, btw (Shocking, I know))
**Client no longer requires EMV-Engine/Console**, which makes it much lighter space/resource wise and hopefully less jarring for the end user. Should also be feature parity between Non/RTX versions, now. This means that every version of RE3Remake should now be completely playable with the randomizer (I don't own the others to test)
**Files can be checks/locations**, they only add junk into the item pool however. Note: If you happened to pick-up any of the files inside the subway station prior to making the save you made to play the randomizer, you'll want to start fresh and make a new save without having done that.
**Added an In-Game Tracker, you can see the locations around you that you've missed** You'll find the toggle inside of the Archipelago Mod Window above the button to re-receive items :)
**Revamped inventory system one more time, so items no longer *have* to be placed into the item box** While making Version 2 last year, I found the actual player fields for Carlos/Jill so I could award items how RE2 does but I had already dumped a ton of time into Version 2 and didn't want to stall the release any further. Note: Items that don't belong to the character being played should go into their respective item box, 2-slot items and weapons still always go to the item box regardless.
**Fixed a major bug with the Lock Pick/Battery Pack** Thanks to everyone who reported this. Previously, if you received the Lock Pick/Battery Pack and then saved/quit/died before seeing the Lock Pick/Battery Pack cutscene, it could disappear from your inventory. It should now persist through save + quit/load/death.
**Electronic Gadget in the R.P.D. is now in the item pool** This means Carlos may finally have to take a break at the police station and eat some donuts. Note: The Electronic Gadget on the Shower Room Wall will look like it enters your inventory, it will disappear afterward immediately. This is to prevent the game from killing the interact to place the bomb afterwards. This was the only solution I could find in my efforts to randomize this location. I'll continue to look into solutions for the Safety Deposit Key and Battery.
**Jewels and the STARS ID Card are now always local** **This prevents players from accidentally disposing of them too early and missing locations later on** You'll always get the Jewels before having to go to the RPD and the ID Card is a requirement to go into the Reception Room from the Main hall in the RPD, so you're guaranteed to get it before it's needed as well (as long as you didn't accidentally skip it somewhere in your own game, which shouldn't be happening anymore :) ) You can still go to the Clock Puzzle when you get to the Subway Station with Carlos and even put the Jewels into the puzzle after that point to so long as you don't accidentally "dispose" of them
**Added two new Traps** (Jill only, unfortunately, because Carlos can't vomit) (I thought of something funny to do as a trap for Carlos, maybe when Version 3 gets officially released)
**Hospital Defense Skip is real(ish)!** You can now sit completely still during that section and it will play out normally Note: You'll still need to place the Detonator in the 2nd phase of the Defense section to trigger the transfer to Jill.
**And a bunch of smaller bug fixes, including:**
Locker 109 is no longer static due to an item_object issue.
Supply Case now correctly give Flame Rounds instead of Acid Rounds.
Locations/Enemies properly sending the first time around. This was a bug in my code in the apworld that went overlooked because I suspected the client was the problem.
Locations/Enemies now have GUIDs attached to them, so you can no longer grab stuff "out of order" accidentally
## Thanks to Fuzzy for the RE2 ported code and this fix as well * Remove likely cause of ImGUI error in recent REF versions - https://github.com/TheRealSolidusSnake/RE3R_AP_Client/pull/7
## What others contributed RopeyRed - Enemy Kills/Files on all difficulties (Standard only this release, however) Grenier - Stripped Scenario/Character out of the client/apworld so it no longer appends (JA), we only append difficulty if it's not a "Standard" location.

entry.title: Haste v0.5.0
entry.content:
The fifth major release of the Haste Archipelago
You will need to subscribe to and enable the [Mod](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3462307025) on Steam.
## New YAML Features - **Disaster Shards** are now supported, acting as Shards 11-14 in the Shard Goal setting - **Starting Shard** allows you to choose which Shard your checks begin in, removing locations in all previous Shards - When playing with Progressive Speed Upgrades, you will be pre-given enough of them to keep up with your Starting Shard - All hub purchases will still expect 1 *additional* Progressive Shard before being logically available - **Dynamic Scaling** for both Shopsanity and Fragmentsanity, which sets the checks in each Shard relative to the length of the Shard itself - The length of each Shard can be found [here](https://github.com/WritingHusky/haste_apworld/blob/main/docs/ShardLengths.md) - **Global Shop Packs** can be added to hard-lock later Global Shopsanity purchases, segmented into blocks of 15 purchases - An additional setting to add extra Packs has also been added - Quality of Life options - **Refund Bad Purchases** will refund you any Sparks spent on *AP Shop Items* that would not send a check. This setting does nothing if you do not have Shopsanity Separate enabled. - **Remove Separate AP Shop Items When Done** will prevent *AP Shop Items* from appearing in Shops once you have exceeded the available checks in that region (either through completely running out, or lacking sufficient Global Shop Packs) - **Scout Hub Locations** enabled all hub purchases to also send AP hints upon opening their respective NPC's dialogue - This setting can be overridden at any time via the in-game options menu. - Anti-Quality of Life option - **Base Disaster Level** will *permanently* set all Shards to have the corresponding Disaster Shard effects - This setting is provided ***WITHOUT ANY SAFEGUARDING LOGIC***. Do NOT enable unless you know what you are doing. - This base Disaster level *will* stack with any Disaster Traps, but will *not* stack with the normal Disaster Shards
## Logic Changes - The Crispy and Twister Flopsy costume purchases have been moved out of Vanilla Plus and into Vanilla, since the Disaster Shards that lock them are now accessible - Expensive Captain's Upgrade and Fashion Weeboh Purchases will require additional Progressive Shards before becoming logically available - Captain's Upgrades: - Purchase 1-2: No additional Shards - Purchase 3-4: 2 additional Shards - Purchase 5: 4 additional Shards - Purchase 6: 6 additional Shards - EXCEPTION: The first and only 'Max Lives' Upgrade purchase expects 2 additional Shards, as it is the same price as Purchase 4 in other upgrade lines - Costume Purchases: - Flopsy and Weeboh: 2 additional Shards - Zoe 64, Twisted Flopsy, and Totally Accurate Zoe: 4 additional Shards
## Bugfixes - Fixed Courier's Board not being considered a valid Ability to access Shards 5 & beyond - Fixed Wraith's Hourglass and Sage's Cowl having swapped IDs in some places, which lead to weird fill errors with the Totally Accurate Zoe costume purchase - Fixed issue where Little Sister and Supersonic Zoe costumes were not being locked properly in Vanilla Plus and All Unlocks - Fixed issue where "Seperate" was used several times instead of "Separate", which is how the word is actually spelled

entry.title: pokemon_stadium v0.8.0
entry.content:
## Reworked move balancing
### The goal of this reworked system is to recreate the difficulty curve of the vanilla game as closely as possible so that players have a sense of progression as they work through a seed
- Removed old system that had 3 different tier systems for physical, special, and status moves - All moves combined into a single tier system now - Assigned "BST modifiers" to each tier. These are used to calculate an "adjusted BST" for each Pokémon - Calculated vanilla adjusted BSTs to and compiled a list of target BSTs for each gym/cup - These target BSTs will get a setting in a later update to allow them to be shuffled - Randomizer now builds movesets for Pokémon that align them with a target BST - Rental lists are sorted by adjusted BST - The later in the rental table a Pokémon appears, the stronger it should be
Also fixed the naming for Poké Cup trainer locations.

> OMF:2097 was released as freeware by Epic MegaGames in 1999. The game data is freely and legally downloadable.
---
### What's New
#### Economy rebalance
Default economy YAML options have been retuned:
- `buy_cost_factor` default doubled, 10 → 20 (Mechlab prices now default to 20% of vanilla, up from 10%) - `money_small_value` default halved, 3000 → 1500 - `money_large_value` default cut to a fifth, 15000 → 3000 - `money_small_step` / `money_large_step` defaults reduced (150 → 100, 750 → 200)
Net effect: purchases cost more relative to money checks by default, and the per-check growth curve is flatter — a tighter default economy. All five remain player-configurable via YAML.
#### Bug fixes (OpenOMF client)
- Fixed the "all tournaments" goal silently failing to complete: winning a tournament wasn't persisted immediately, so the mechlab's save-reload on entry could clobber the just-won tournament bit before it was written to disk - Fixed forfeiting a match in Archipelago mode sometimes being scored using stale data from the previous match
#### Testing
- AP-specific tests now build as their own `openomf_test_ap` binary (they link Archipelago-only symbols), instead of living inside the main test suite - New test coverage for the tournament-goal logic (`AP Tournament Goal` suite)
---

# Diablo II Archipelago — Unstable 3.6.4
## The channel is now called Unstable
It used to say "Stable". That promised more than it should: this is a project that ships fixes the same day they are found, and several releases in a day is normal. "Unstable" is the honest label.
Nothing about how it works has changed. In game the version reads `U-3.6.4` — the slot Diablo II gives us holds eleven characters, and the full word does not fit next to a version number.
## The Treasure Cow is a real super-unique now
**Every cow in the Cow Level was called "Archipelago Treasure Cow".** That was not a display bug — the Treasure Cow was an ordinary Hell Bovine, and the only way to give it a name was to rename the monster *type* in the string table. That renames every Hell Bovine in the game, all thousands of them.
So the Treasure Cow got its own entry in the super-unique table, and the Hell Bovine has its vanilla name back. **The Cow Level reads normally again.**
The cow still comes alone, still hits like a boss, and it can appear more than once in a session.
## Killing it drops chests
The cow used to pay out by handing items straight to you, which is where every "the cow dropped nothing" report came from. It now spawns **3 to 5 sparkling chests** around you instead, and Diablo II's own chest code does the rest:
- every item rolls at magic quality, 5% of the time rare - they skip the 25% "drops nothing" gate an ordinary chest has to pass - if nothing magic came out, the game rerolls up to ten more times
A sparkling chest cannot come up empty. That guarantee is the game's, not ours.
If the mod does not recognise your game build it quietly falls back to the old item reward rather than spawning nothing, and says so in the log.
## Testing it
The cheat menu (Ctrl+V) has a **Treasure Cow** button under Mons → Bosses, so you can spawn one where you stand instead of waiting for it to turn up.
## Source code
The full source is now on GitHub alongside the release, for both this line and the experimental one.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.6.5
entry.content:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Unstable 3.6.5
## The cheat menu fits the screen now
Some tabs — Runes, Gems and Misc under Loot — were taller than the screen at 800x600. The panel centred itself on its own height, so on those tabs the title bar with the close button sat up to 67 pixels above the top edge and the last rows below the bottom one, with no way to reach either.
The panel now caps its height to the screen and the content scrolls instead: mouse wheel over the panel, scrollbar on the right edge, and each tab remembers its own position. Tabs that fit are unchanged.
## Choose how many skills are in the pool
New option in both the Archipelago YAML (**Skill Pool Size**) and the launcher's standalone settings (a checkbox plus a slider). Off, or 0, means what it has always meant: every skill that passes the class filter.
Set it to 30 and the pool is exactly 30 skills — **10 tier-1, 10 tier-2 and 10 tier-3, picked at random**. The split stays even at any value, the class filter is applied first, and the skill locations that no longer hold a skill fill with ordinary filler instead.
## Tested
This release went through the full logic battery: every option at both extremes, the risky combinations (gates x entrances x goals, now including the new pool cap against all of them), 300 randomised option sets, a mixed multiworld, all 56 custom goals, a 126-slot world with ~300,000 foreign locations, and the gate-key placement audit — 360 key placements, none unreachable. The sweep also caught two real bugs in this feature before release, which is exactly what it is for.
## Launcher 2.9.35
- **Volume slider** for the notification sounds, defaulting to 50%. - **Add your own sound** — pick a wav, mp3 or wma and it appears in the per-event sound lists. Your files live in their own folder that updates never touch.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.6.6
entry.content:
# Unstable 3.6.6
Rewards you can plan around. 33 new filler items, and where they land now depends on how far into the run you are.
## Tiered rewards land at a matching depth
High runes, perfect gems, grand charms and the big point items are held back for the later acts and difficulties. Their low-tier counterparts come early. A Vex is no longer exactly as likely in Blood Moor as in Hell Act 5.
Measured over a full seed: **100% of tiered rewards now land inside their band, against 62-66% before.**
The bands scale to the seed. A Full Normal run only spans Act 1 through Act 5 Normal, so the whole ladder is squeezed onto that — the order survives even when "late" means Act 4 Normal instead of Act 3 Hell.
New option **Tiered Filler Depth** (on by default) in both the AP YAML and the standalone settings. Turn it off for the old flat roll. It only moves filler, so logic and reachability are identical either way.
## New rewards
**Tiered bundles** — Random Rune (Mid), Random Rune (High), Flawless Gem, Perfect Gem, Small Charm, Large Charm, Grand Charm. The high rune band runs Pul through Ohm; Lo and above stay out of the filler pool.
**Point items in real sizes** — 1, 3 and 10 Stat Points; 1, 2 and 3 Skill Points; 1 and 3 Reset Points. Named honestly, so what the multiworld shows other players is what you actually receive.
**Gear by slot** — set and unique drops split into armour, helm, shield, gloves, boots, belt, weapon and jewelry. "Drop: Unique Boots" now means boots.
## New traps
- **Barrel Field** — a ring of exploding barrels around you - **Urn Garden** — a floor of urns to wade through - **False Treasure** — six chests, two of which are not chests - **Junk Backpack** — twenty useless items into your pack
The first three hold until you leave town. All four also appear in standalone runs.
## Fixes
- **Standalone was missing twelve reward types.** The ordinary-item bundles added in 3.6.5 were only ever wired into the Archipelago roll — a standalone character could never receive them. All 19 bundles and all 8 trap types now roll in both modes. - The Treasure Cow's chests and the new object traps now share one spawner instead of two copies of the same code.
## Verified
Generation checked across the smoke, isolate, risky and multiworld option sweeps in both lines. A 300-player multiworld generated clean: 522 gate keys placed, zero depth violations.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.6.7
entry.content:
# Unstable 3.6.7
A loot filter. Choose what colour each kind of drop is drawn in, or stop drawing it at all.
## Where
**Launcher → Settings → Diablo II → Loot Filter → "Colours and hiding…"**
Twenty-two groups, each with a colour and a Hide box:
**By type** — gold, runes, gems, charms, jewels, rings and amulets, health and mana potions, rejuvenation, throwing potions, antidote/thawing/stamina, scrolls, tomes, keys, arrows and bolts, quest items.
**By quality** — normal, superior, magic, rare, set, unique, crafted.
Ten colours: white, red, green, blue, gold, grey, tan, orange, yellow, or Default to leave it exactly as the game draws it.
Everything starts at Default, so if you never open the dialog nothing about your game changes. The setting is remembered across seeds and applies to both Archipelago and standalone runs.
Gold as orange, runes in their own colour, plain white gear gone entirely — whatever you want.
## Read this before you turn it on
**This is the first release of the filter and it is not fully proven.**
Diablo II does not keep item colours in any data file; it decides them in code. The only way to change them is to intercept the game's drawing calls, and that interception sees *every* piece of text the game client draws — menus and shop lists included, not just labels on the ground.
There is a guard: a rule only applies to text that arrived with a backdrop behind it, which ground labels have and menu text does not. It should be enough. It has not been confirmed in a real session.
So: if you set a rule and text goes missing somewhere it should not, that is this. Open the dialog and press **Reset all to default** — it takes effect on the next launch, no reinstall and no waiting for a patch.
There is a **"Log every item label"** box at the bottom of the dialog. Turning it on for a minute and sending the resulting `d2arch_log.txt` is what will settle whether the guard holds.
## Also
The mod's import-patching helper now handles ordinal imports, which is how the Diablo II modules export nearly everything. That is what made the filter reachable at all.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.6.8
entry.content:
# Unstable 3.6.8
## The loot filter is gone again
3.6.7 added a filter for recolouring and hiding item labels on the ground. It did not work, and it is removed.
The honest version of what happened: Diablo II decides those colours in code rather than in any data file, so changing them means intercepting the game's drawing calls. Which call to intercept could not be established from the binary — the function that reads the Alt key, which is the one that decides whether to label items at all, makes no drawing call anywhere near itself. The release went out on a reasonable guess with a fallback plan, and the fallback is this patch.
Nothing else in 3.6.7 was affected, and nothing carried over: the mod no longer contains the code, and the launcher writes the filter off on every launch so a mismatched pair of versions cannot leave it running.
Everything from 3.6.6 — tiered reward depth, the 33 new filler items, the four object traps — is untouched.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.6.9
entry.content:
# Unstable 3.6.9
Debug menu (Ctrl+V), Character tab.
## Two new buttons
**+100M XP** — exactly one hundred million experience. From a fresh character that lands you at level 57.
**Max Level** — straight to 99. There because 100M is not actually enough to reach the Pandemonium content: from level 90 it does not even give you one more level.
Both stop at 99 rather than doing anything, and say so in the log.
## +10 Levels now gives ten levels
It used to hand over a flat 500,000 experience regardless of where you were. That is roughly thirty levels at level 1 and next to nothing at level 80 — the button had been lying about what it did.
It now reads your level and adds the actual gap to level+10.
## Under the hood
Level 99 costs 3,837,739,017 experience, which does not fit in the signed 32-bit value the game's stat call takes. A large grant is handed over in pieces, and never more than the room left below the cap — adding past it wraps the total negative, and the character would look like it had lost every level it had.
Launcher unchanged at 2.9.38.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.0
entry.content:
# v3.7.0
## The version is just a number now
No more Beta, Stable or Unstable. Each of those made a promise about the build that the number already says better, and the last rename was itself a reaction to "Stable" claiming too much. A bare version claims nothing.
`Unstable-3.6.9` was the last of the old spelling; this is `v3.7.0`.
## Hunts now say where the target actually is
With the super-unique shuffle on, a hunt's target keeps its name but stands on some other boss's spawn point. Three separate displays were supposed to tell you that. None of them did, for three different reasons:
**The quest book showed nothing at all.** The code that looks up the moved target's real location sat behind a condition that could never be true — the line above it had already ruled out every hunt. It was dead from the day it was written.
**Zone names were off by one.** The area name table is indexed by area id directly, but the book read it one slot low, so every zone on the page named its neighbour. This is very likely why the hunt areas were written off as untrustworthy at the time: the table was right, the reading was wrong.
**The in-game tracker named the host but not the place.** It now says both.
A hunt reads `Found in: Black Marsh (at Rakanishu's spot)` when shuffled, and its own verified zone when not.
## Boss loot was invisible in solo runs
Every reward type announces itself so the launcher can log it and play a sound. Boss loot said "Awesome loot incoming!", which carried none of the markers the solo pipe filters on — so it produced no tracker entry and no sound, and always had. It now announces itself like everything else: `Drop: Andariel Loot (4 items)`.
Traps had the same problem and are fixed alongside.
## Debug menu
Unchanged from 3.6.9: `+100M XP`, `Max Level`, and `+10 Levels` giving ten actual levels.
Requires launcher 2.9.39.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.1
entry.content:
# v3.7.1 — Crash & stability round (safe mid-run)
Every fix in this release is runtime-only: nothing changes the generated world, the check list, or item placement. It is safe to update in the middle of an ongoing multiworld — that is the whole point of it.
## Crash fixes
- **Fixed the "cow crash"** (assertion in UnitRoom.cpp / DungeonTestRoomGame). Every spawn the mod performs — Treasure Cow, cow hoard chests, trap ambushes, object traps — now resolves the room that actually CONTAINS the target coordinates before spawning. Previously the player's own room was passed with far-away coordinates, and the game asserts on that mismatch instead of failing gracefully; the cow's "30 placement attempts" never got a second try. The cow also spawns closer now (25-100 yards instead of 40-300), so its placement lands inside loaded terrain. - **Fixed the texture-cache crash** (glTextureCache.cpp / tTempItem). Object traps (barrels / urns / false treasure) only spawn object types that are already present in the area around you — an act-foreign object has no loaded graphics and killed the renderer. A trap that cannot fire safely fizzles silently instead of crashing.
## Traps
- **A "Trap: Monsters" filler no longer announces itself as the Monster Revive Trap.** The ambush queue now remembers who queued it: reward traps say "TRAP! Monsters incoming!", only the actual Revive Trap says "The slain rise against you!". (The Revive Trap toggle itself always worked — the message was lying.)
## Item delivery / progression
- **Raised both redelivery-protection caps** (applied-item ids 4096 → 16384, filler locations 2048 → 8192) and made hitting a cap log loudly. Anything that fell off these lists silently was re-delivered on the next reconnect — the "save & quit gave me 28 skill points" report. - **Settings now survive save & load correctly:** `xp_multiplier` was clamped by a leftover 1-10 guard on load (the setting goes 0-100 — an x25 player lost the multiplier every restart), and `skill_max_level` + `skill_level_reqs` were written to the state file but never read back.
## Gameplay
- **Treasure Cow rebalanced:** max 3 per act (was 5), 8% chance per area (was 25%), and early-act HP bonuses roughly halved. A boss-tier cow in Den of Evil at level 1 was not a fair fight. `treasure_cows.dat` overrides still apply if present. - **After a crash you can no longer keep a skill you don't own on left/right click** — the mod now validates hand-assigned skills continuously and resets unowned ones to Attack. - **One kill can no longer complete two Hunts.** A super-unique's minions share the boss's class, and the class-match fallback credited the minions' hunt on top of the boss's own — minions and champions are now excluded from fallback crediting. - **Clear Monastery Gate / Clear Inner Cloister** are now reach-the-area checks. Those zones spawn almost no monsters, so "kill 8" meant dragging monsters in from next door. Same treatment as the Tower Cellar fix in 3.0.0.
## Entrance shuffle
- **Exiting a cross-act shuffled dungeon returns you to the entrance you came from** instead of bouncing you town-to-town. The act-town lock used to wipe the recorded way home (this is what broke the Cain quest for one player), and zone-locking could override the return warp in the same tick. The original entrance always wins now.
## UI
- **The HUD tracker no longer draws on top of the open Book.**

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.2
entry.content:
# v3.7.2 — Settings, gold and a stuck-skill rescue (safe mid-run)
Game-side only. The launcher is unchanged (still 2.9.39), and so is every generated data file — **your monsters, bosses, entrances and vendors stay exactly where they are.** Safe to install in the middle of a run.
## Your settings actually apply now
- **Skill point cap was stuck at 20** no matter what your YAML said. The value arrived correctly from the server, then the character's own saved state overwrote it with a stale one. Under Archipelago the YAML is now the final word; standalone keeps its per-character settings as before. Same fix for "skill level requirements". No cleanup needed — it corrects itself on load.
## Gold
- **Gold rewards announced "0 Gold" while paying the real amount.** When gold became level-scaled the amount moved to where the character's level is known, but the message stayed behind and kept printing a hardcoded zero. You were always being paid; only the text lied. - *Experimental line only:* level-scaled gold was queued but **never actually granted** — four places added to the queue and nothing ever emptied it.
## Quality of life
- **Whirlwind (and any skill with its own animation) no longer traps you.** Start one holding a bow, crossbow or spear and the character used to freeze until you logged out. If you are stuck in a skill animation and haven't moved for three seconds, the game now nudges you free by itself. - **The "SOMETHING UNUSUAL IS NEARBY" warning** lost its black box — it was sized by guessing the pixel width from the character count, so it only ever covered the first half of the message. The text is also higher and further left. Both offsets are tunable in `d2arch.ini` under `[Notifications]` (`BigWarnOffsetX`, `BigWarnOffsetY`).
## Items
- **Quest items can no longer be handed out as random unique or set drops.** Six quest bases were reachable this way — the Viper Amulet, Khalim's Flail and Will, the Staff of Kings, the Horadric Staff and the Hellforge Hammer. Getting a spare could confuse or break the chain it belongs to. - **Every super-unique the mod adds has a real name.** All 45 showed up as "an evil force", which is also why a gate guardian standing next to its quest boss looked like a broken duplicate. They now read "Gatekeeper <name>", so you can tell the key-holder from the real thing.
## Not in this release
The monster, super-unique and shop shuffle rebalances are built and tested but deliberately held back: they change the generated world, and that would move things around mid-run. They ship once the current games are finished.
